Market Mastery Webinar by Vishal Malkan Find the weak links in your portfolio by Vishal Malkan Register for FREE Webinar Register for FREE Chennai-based Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) startup SuperOps has laid off around 60 employees from its engineering team of nearly 100 people, as part of an internal restructuring exercise aimed at improving efficiency, sources told Moneycontrol. The layoffs, which account for roughly 30 percent of SuperOps’ overall workforce, come as the company shifts towards becoming an AI-first organisation. The move signals a strategic change in how the startup plans to build and deliver its IT operations and MSP (managed service provider) solutions, with a sharper focus on automation and AI-led product development. SuperOps confirmed the developments to Moneycontrol. Sources said the decision was not driven by financial stress but by the need to realign teams and resources in line with its evolving product roadmap. Here's what HDFC AMC's Navneet Munot thinks “This is purely for efficiency as we transition into an AI-first company,” a source close to the development told Moneycontrol. Affected employees have been provided severance packages and job-seeking support, including connections, to ensure a smoother transition. As part of this transition, SuperOps is also setting up a dedicated internal AI council, expected to comprise 10 to 20 members. This team will focus on embedding AI capabilities across the company’s product stack, as well as driving experimentation and faster deployment of AI features. Founded in 2020 by Arvind Parthiban and Jayakumar Karumbasalam, SuperOps provides an AI-powered IT management platform for managed service providers and internal IT teams. The restructuring comes shortly after the company raised $25 million in a Series C funding round led by March Capital, with participation from Addition and Z47, taking its total funding to about $54.4 million to date. The move comes amid a broader trend across the global technology industry, where companies are restructuring teams to prioritise AI capabilities. Firms such as Salesforce, Google, and Amazon have in recent months undertaken layoffs or role reallocations while simultaneously increasing investments in AI and automation, reflecting a wider shift in how tech companies are deploying talent and resources.
